title: Closing a Pending Estimate Month Against Its Cost of Care: Medical Assistance Calculation Standard
content:
Under Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage, the reduction on a closed estimate month of a pending case is figured as follows.

1. **Month and estimate.** The review covers the calendar month before the current month on a case that is pending, and the case's patient pay charge billed as an estimate (charge basis "estimated pending") for that service month. The estimate for the month is the amount billed on that charge less the reductions already posted for that service month. Where no such charge was billed, or the case is not in status pending, the reduction is zero.

2. **Day-by-day pricing applies** where a pending accrual is posted for the month, the bed-hold days booked for the month all belong to one bed-hold reservation, the month's Part A days were all booked by the resident's coverage with the latest coverage start, and every day of the month is accounted for once — the days in the center that the month's pending accrual counts, the bed-hold days booked for the month less the days reversed from those bookings, the days with no bed held, the days before a skilled admission inside the month and the days after a held bed's last held day inside the month where the hospital discharged the resident elsewhere add up to the month's calendar days.
   - The days with no bed held, counted as far as they fall in the month and each up to the day before the return (to the month's end where the resident has not come back): from the leave start of the resident's latest declined reservation (by leave start); after the last held day of the latest reservation that ended because the payer's reserved days were used with no private extension (by end date); after the release of the latest released reservation (by release date); after the last held day of the latest private hold that ended unpaid or at its maximum (by end date, the one that ended unpaid where both share the latest end date).
   - A skilled admission is the resident's Medicare coverage with the latest coverage start date beginning inside the month on the day its qualifying hospital stay ended; the held bed is the resident's latest-ending reservation that ended because the hospital discharged the resident elsewhere.

3. **Otherwise** the cost of care is the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, rounded half up to the cent, the days in the center being those the month's pending accrual counts, or every calendar day where no accrual was posted; a month of admission, discharge or death takes its patient pay under the partial-month rule (the lesser of the monthly patient pay and the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate).

4. **Day-by-day cost of care.** Every calendar day of the month is priced at the Medicaid daily rate on the case, except that the Part A days Medicare covers in full (days booked for the month in benefit days 1 through 20, less the days reversed from those bookings) and the days a lapsed physician certification leaves to the center (days reversed as uncertified days from the month's bookings) carry no cost, and the Part A coinsurance days (days booked for the month in benefit days 21 through 100, less the days reversed from those bookings) are priced at the highest daily coinsurance booked for them. Days at the daily rate are the calendar days neither taken out nor priced as coinsurance days, never fewer than zero; each kind of day is priced and rounded half up to the cent, and the priced kinds are added.

5. **Reduction.** The estimate for the month less that cost of care, never below zero, rounded half up to the cent, posted against that estimate with reason "cost-of-care cap". Where two records share the latest date a reading goes by, the one posted first is read.

**Hypothetical worked figure.** A 31-day pending month priced day by day; Medicaid daily rate 247.35 dollars; estimate 2,615.40 dollars with no reduction yet; a skilled stay whose benefit days 1 through 20 fall on days 1 to 20 of the month and whose benefit days 21 through 25 fall on days 21 to 25, booked at a daily coinsurance of 209.50 dollars, with no day reversed; Part A coverage ended after day 25. Days at the daily rate: 31 less 20 less 5, which is 6 days, 1,484.10 dollars; coinsurance days 5 at 209.50, 1,047.50 dollars; cost of care 2,531.60 dollars; reduction 2,615.40 less 2,531.60, which is 83.80 dollars. In another pending month, a month of admission not priced day by day whose pending accrual counts 6 days in the center, an estimate of 2,615.40 dollars against a cost of care of 6 days at 247.35 dollars, 1,484.10 dollars, gives a reduction of 1,131.30 dollars.
